gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BLUETTI AC180 (1,152 Wh) is in stock at $499 on BLUETTI's US store as of 2026-11-14, when runtimemath lists it as a pre-order shipping Dec 14 and ChatGPT called it limited. None of them lists the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Classic (1,024 Wh, 1,800 W) at $459 on EcoFlow's US store, the cheapest roughly 1 kWh station found on any maker store checked today.
standout_why: I compared against runtimemath.com (ranked #2, not cited), blackoutwise.com (cited) and wattfort.com (cited). Runtimemath already prices 18 models with maker prices dated Nov 9, including AC180 $499, Elite 100 V2 $499, Elite 30 V2 $289.99 and C1000 Gen 2 $499.99, and gives idle draw for 7 of them. So prices alone are mostly covered. What runtimemath lacks is today's stock: it shows the AC180 as a pre-order shipping Dec 14, and BLUETTI shows every AC180 variant available today. It also leaves out the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Classic ($459) and the RIVER 2 Pro ($369 and in stock, while ChatGPT's card said out of stock). Blackoutwise and wattfort print no prices at all.
decides: This confirms the AC180 as the pick for a typical 120 V blanket and takes away the stock caveat ChatGPT added. At $499 it is in stock today, gives the most Wh per dollar among in-stock 1 kWh-class units at maker stores, and its arithmetic covers about 83 W average for 10 h. The DELTA 3 Classic is $40 cheaper but has 128 Wh less and no idle figure I could source. The Elite 100 V2 costs the same $499 for 128 Wh less. Anker's store search shows the C1000 Gen 2 at $699.99 today. For a queen blanket at Cockeyed's measured 115 W on low (cited by wattfort), no 1 kWh unit lasts 10 h. That pushes the buyer to the 2 kWh class: Jackery 2000 v2 at $999 (pre-order, ships Nov 16) or EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max Plus at $1,149 (in stock). For 12 V blankets, the Elite 30 V2 at $289.99 stays the budget pick.
